item: Row 304: the vacuum reports what the disk got back on a write-ahead-log store
summary: On a WAL store neither vacuum returns space to the disk at once: freed pages wait for a checkpoint, and a reader holds that back. Measured on plain and encrypted stores: incremental_vacuum frees every requested page even with a reader holding a snapshot (the old 'reader blocks it' wording was rollback-journal behaviour); a full VACUUM with no reader shrinks the file only once the log crosses the automatic checkpoint, while the log holds the same bytes, and with a reader the file is unchanged and the log is added on top. bytes_reclaimed is now the measured fall in file plus -wal (None when unreadable, never 0); bytes freed inside the database that the disk has not seen are reported apart as freed_not_yet_shrunk with the reason; pages_reclaimed is renamed pages_freed. Settings now says 'Space returned to the disk' and shows the pending bytes on their own line (x12); the disk is measured inside the write gate; disk growth is stated as bytes_added_on_disk. No forced checkpoint, nothing rebuilt.
